This book is a comprehensive course in statistical machine learning. It
is organized as a single sequence that combines concepts, reproducible
examples, and guided analysis.

The course is organized around a practical sequence:

1. Build statistical learning intuition from prediction, inference, and
   model error.
2. Use linear models as the first complete workflow for estimation,
   interpretation, diagnostics, and generalization.
3. Extend regression through interactions, classification, logistic
   regression, discriminant analysis, resampling, feature engineering,
   model selection, regularization, dimension reduction, nonlinear
   regression, trees, ensembles, support vector machines, and
   unsupervised learning.
4. End with reproducible model development, applied case studies, and
   the judgment needed to teach or deploy statistical learning
   responsibly.
